hot.title: Unlimited OCR Works
hot.summary: Unlimited OCR introduces a model for one-shot, long-horizon parsing of multi-page documents, employing a Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA) mechanism to maintain a constant KV cache size and stable inference speed. The model achieved an overall score of 93.23% on OmniDocBench v1.5, representing a 6.22 percentage point improvement over its baseline, while efficiently processing continuous document streams.

hot.title: Tmax: A Simple Recipe for Terminal Agents
hot.summary: Researchers at Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington introduce TMAX, a novel dataset and an effective reinforcement learning recipe for training open-weight language models as terminal agents. TMAX-9B achieved 27.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, outperforming prior open-weight models under 10B parameters and demonstrating robust generalization across various agentic tasks and evaluation harnesses.

hot.title: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents
hot.summary: Qwen-AgentWorld introduces a family of language world models (LWMs) that simulate diverse agentic environments, surpassing frontier LLMs on the AgentWorldBench and improving agent performance across various downstream tasks. These models enhance agent learning through scalable, controllable simulation and by integrating internal predictive reasoning for action refinement.

hot.title: ParallelKernelBench: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels?
hot.summary: ParallelKernelBench (PKB), a new benchmark and evaluation framework, assesses the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate high-performance multi-GPU kernels. The evaluation shows frontier LLMs struggle with complex distributed parallelism, achieving limited correctness and speedup in single-shot settings, though they occasionally produce 'net new' kernels that outperform PyTorch+NCCL baselines for specific workloads.

hot.title: Tapered Language Models
hot.summary: This work introduces Tapered Language Models (TLMs), an architectural principle that monotonically decreases a parameter-bearing component's capacity, specifically MLP width, across model depth while maintaining a fixed total parameter budget. The approach consistently improved average commonsense reasoning accuracy and perplexity across diverse architectures and scales, achieving up to 1.84 perplexity points improvement on a 440M Transformer compared to uniform baselines.

hot.title: HoloAgent-0: A Unified Embodied Agent Framework with 3D Spatial Memory
hot.summary: HoloAgent-0, a unified embodied agent framework developed by Horizon Robotics and D-Robotics Robotics, bridges the divide between large language model reasoning and real-world physical robot execution. It integrates persistent 3D spatial memory and a structured skill interface to facilitate robust, closed-loop task execution, demonstrating high success rates in real-robot navigation and competitive performance in semantic mapping.

hot.title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence
hot.summary: S-AGENT introduces a framework for spatial intelligence in Vision-Language Models, enabling them to reason over continuous, evolving 3D environments by accumulating spatio-temporal evidence. This is achieved through a VLM planner orchestrating hierarchical spatial tools and dual memory systems, leading to improved performance on multi-image and video spatial reasoning benchmarks.

hot.title: MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?
hot.summary: A new benchmark, MAS-PromptBench, systematically quantifies the effects of prompt optimization in multi-agent LLM systems, revealing that while optimization can improve performance by up to 24.0 percentage points in specific setups, it can also cause degradations of up to 16.0 points, with outcomes heavily influenced by task type, communication structure, and team size.

hot.title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
hot.summary: INSIGHT introduces a framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to autonomously acquire new manipulation skills by identifying missing primitive actions and generating their own training data. The system enables robots to continually expand their learned skill vocabulary, achieving high success rates in novel tasks while retaining prior capabilities and improving execution efficiency.

hot.title: Tmax: A simple recipe for terminal agents
hot.summary: Researchers at the Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington developed TMAX-15K, a large and diverse dataset of complex terminal tasks, alongside a simple reinforcement learning (RL) training recipe for open-weight language models. This approach enabled TMAX-9B to achieve 27.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, making it the top-performing open-weight model under 10 billion parameters at the time of publication and surpassing several larger models.

hot.title: Agent-as-a-Router: Agentic Model Routing for Coding Tasks
hot.summary: A collaborative research team introduced Agent-as-a-Router, an adaptive framework that dynamically selects the most suitable large language model for coding tasks by learning from execution-grounded feedback through a Context-Action-Feedback (C-A-F) loop. This approach yielded higher average performance and lower cumulative regret on diverse coding tasks, demonstrating improved cost-efficiency compared to static routing and fixed-model strategies.

hot.title: SeFi-Image: A Text-to-Image Foundation Model with Semantic-First Diffusion
hot.summary: A text-to-image foundation model, SEFI-IMAGE, employs Semantic-First Diffusion (SFD) to achieve performance comparable to or exceeding state-of-the-art models while utilizing approximately 10-20% of their training computational resources. This model demonstrates improved capabilities in handling long-text rendering and visual text generation.

hot.title: MeshFlow: Mesh Generation with Equivariant Flow Matching
hot.summary: MeshFlow generates high-quality 3D triangle meshes using an equivariant optimal-transport flow matching model applied to a triangle soup representation. The method achieves an 18.55x speedup over autoregressive baselines, generating meshes in under a second, while improving fidelity and reducing self-intersections to 7.97% on categories like Lamp.

hot.title: CLI-Universe: Towards Verifiable Task Synthesis Engine for Terminal Agents
hot.summary: CLI-Universe introduces a synthesis engine designed to create high-quality, verifiable training tasks for LLM-based terminal agents, addressing the challenge of limited, ambiguous training data. The generated CLI-Universe-6K dataset enables a Qwen3-32B model to achieve a 33.4% pass rate on Terminal-Bench 2.0, outperforming other open-source models of comparable size and several larger open-weight models.

hot.title: SPIRAL: Learning to Search and Aggregate
hot.summary: The SPIRAL framework trains large language models to optimize the combined use of sequential, parallel, and aggregative inference compute end-to-end. This approach yields models that achieve up to 11x higher scaling efficiency in pass@k and 13.5% greater performance with recursive self-aggregation on mathematical reasoning tasks.

hot.title: Deeper is Not Always Better: Mitigating the Alignment Tax via Confident Layer Decoding
hot.summary: Researchers from Alibaba's Qwen Team, Tsinghua University, and Nanyang Technological University developed Confident Decoding, a training-free strategy that dynamically selects an optimal near-final layer for next-token prediction in large language models. This approach consistently improved performance on complex reasoning benchmarks across various architectures, addressing the "alignment tax" where final layers sometimes perturb refined reasoning towards generic or alignment-preferred tokens.

hot.title: Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild
hot.summary: Carnegie Mellon University researchers developed Lift4D, a test-time optimization framework that reconstructs complete 4D (3D geometry and motion) representations of dynamic, non-rigid objects from monocular in-the-wild videos. The system integrates causal latent propagation for temporal consistency and occlusion-aware appearance refinement with view-conditioned diffusion priors, demonstrating improved perceptual quality, temporal coherence, and semantic fidelity over prior methods on synthetic and real-world datasets.

hot.title: World Action Models: A Survey
hot.summary: The survey by Shen et al. addresses the inconsistent terminology and blurred boundaries in the rapidly evolving field of World Action Models (WAMs) in embodied AI. It provides a systematic framework, classifying WAMs into three design philosophies and a four-axis component-level anatomy, revealing pervasive design trade-offs between representational richness and computational efficiency.

hot.title: SingGuard: A Policy-Adaptive Multimodal LLM Guardrail with Dynamic Reasoning
hot.summary: The SingGuard framework, developed by the AI Security Lab at Ant Group, introduces a policy-adaptive multimodal LLM guardrail that dynamically assesses safety in VLM interactions by interpreting active policies as runtime inputs. It achieved state-of-the-art average F1 scores across six benchmark families, notably a 0.9092 macro-average F1 on multimodal safety benchmarks, while supporting flexible inference regimes for practical deployment.

hot.title: AdaReP:Adaptive Re-Planning under Model Mismatch for Neural World-Model Predictive Control
hot.summary: AdaReP introduces an adaptive re-planning framework for neural world-model predictive control, dynamically adjusting the replanning frequency based on online observable signals. The method significantly reduces planner-side computation, achieving over 80% fewer world-model queries in real-world robotic tasks, while maintaining task performance comparable to continuous replanning.

likes.title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence
likes.summary: S-AGENT introduces a framework for spatial intelligence in Vision-Language Models, enabling them to reason over continuous, evolving 3D environments by accumulating spatio-temporal evidence. This is achieved through a VLM planner orchestrating hierarchical spatial tools and dual memory systems, leading to improved performance on multi-image and video spatial reasoning benchmarks.

likes.title: Tmax: A Simple Recipe for Terminal Agents
likes.summary: Researchers at Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington introduce TMAX, a novel dataset and an effective reinforcement learning recipe for training open-weight language models as terminal agents. TMAX-9B achieved 27.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, outperforming prior open-weight models under 10B parameters and demonstrating robust generalization across various agentic tasks and evaluation harnesses.

likes.title: Do as I Do: Dexterous Manipulation Data from Everyday Human Videos
likes.summary: The DO AS I DO algorithm generates dexterous manipulation data for multi-fingered robots by reconstructing 3D hand-object interactions from everyday monocular human videos and retargeting them into executable robot actions. This approach achieved a 71% success rate on reconstructed in-the-wild trajectories and demonstrated real-world execution across diverse tasks.

likes.title: MemoryWAM: Efficient World Action Modeling with Persistent Memory
likes.summary: A hybrid memory design is presented for World Action Models, enabling efficient and persistent long-range context for robotic manipulation in memory-dependent tasks. This approach achieves comparable or superior performance to full-history models on benchmarks like RMBench and real-world scenarios while significantly reducing inference latency and GPU memory consumption.

likes.title: MolmoMotion: Forecasting Point Trajectories in 3D with Language Instruction
likes.summary: The Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington developed MolmoMotion, a system that forecasts object-attached 3D point trajectories in world coordinates, conditioned on language instructions and visual history. This method improved robot manipulation task success rates by over 20 percentage points and enhanced video generation realism, outperforming existing motion prediction baselines on a new 3D motion benchmark.

likes.title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
likes.summary: Engels et al. (2026) investigate the transparency of DiffusionGemma, a text diffusion model, finding it achieves comparable monitorability to autoregressive models like Gemma 4. The study demonstrates that its latent intermediate states can be made largely interpretable, significantly reducing its 'opaque serial depth' and revealing unique non-autoregressive reasoning patterns.

likes.title: ImageWAM: Do World Action Models Really Need Video Generation, or Just Image Editing?
likes.summary: ImageWAM reconfigures pretrained image editing models to act as efficient visual backbones for robot action prediction, demonstrating that compact, instruction-conditioned visual transformation representations can replace full video generation in World Action Models. This approach achieved up to 93.56% success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 83.1% on LIBERO-Plus, while reducing inference latency by approximately 75% and computational FLOPs by about 83% compared to video-generation WAMs.

likes.title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
likes.summary: WRBench, a diagnostic benchmark for evaluating video generation models, reveals that current systems struggle to maintain a consistently evolving world state independent of observation. It exposes a "preservation–access–re-observed-consistency gap," where models often fail to correctly advance object states and events when out of view, performing as "tracking shots" instead of genuine world models.

likes.title: VIMPO: Value-Implicit Policy Optimization for LLMs
likes.summary: VIMPO introduces a policy optimization framework for large language models that bridges the simplicity of critic-free methods with the fine-grained credit assignment of actor-critic approaches. The method, developed at UC Berkeley and Yale, achieves higher validation accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks and demonstrates greater robustness to noisy reward signals compared to existing critic-free baselines.

likes.title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
likes.summary: A study empirically compares egocentric human video and real-robot data for embodied pretraining, demonstrating that human video yields superior generalization to unseen tasks and enhanced robustness in real-world robot deployment, even with pseudo-action labels. The research finds that egocentric data scales predictably and fosters a more effective "open-world prior" for robotic policies.

likes.title: Playful Agentic Robot Learning
likes.summary: A multi-agent Code-as-Policy system, RATS, enables robots to autonomously acquire reusable skills through self-directed play. The system improved average task success rates by 20.6 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO and 17.0 percentage points on MolmoSpaces, and demonstrated effective sim-to-real and cross-environment skill transfer.

likes.title: AtomMem: Building Simple and Effective Memory System for LLM Agents via Atomic Facts
likes.summary: Researchers from the University of Science and Technology of China developed AtomMem, a long-term memory system for LLM agents that extracts and organizes atomic facts hierarchically with graph-based associative recall. The system achieved state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks like LoCoMo, demonstrating improved complex reasoning and reducing API token consumption by approximately 61.4%.

likes.title: FAPO: Fully Automated Prompt Optimization of Multi-Step LLM Pipelines
likes.summary: The FAPO framework introduces a fully automated system for optimizing multi-step LLM pipelines, enabling an orchestrator LLM to diagnose failures at intermediate steps and propose targeted interventions, including prompt adjustments, chain parameter modifications, or structural changes. It demonstrates a mean performance gain of +14.1 percentage points over prior methods by escalating beyond prompt-only optimizations.

likes.title: ENPIRE: Agentic Robot Policy Self-Improvement in the Real World
likes.summary: ENPIRE provides a framework for autonomous robot policy self-improvement, allowing coding agents to refine dexterous manipulation skills directly on physical robots without extensive human supervision. The system achieves up to 99% success rates on challenging real-world tasks like pin insertion and zip-tie cutting, utilizing automated environment feedback and parallelized learning across robot fleets.

likes.title: Native Active Perception as Reasoning for Omni-Modal Understanding
likes.summary: OmniAgent, a framework for multimodal large language models, enables scalable understanding of long-form videos by reformulating perception as an iterative reasoning process, distilling transient multimodal data into a persistent textual memory. It sets new state-of-the-art recall accuracy across ten omni-modal benchmarks, including a 50.5% accuracy on LVBench, while demonstrating greater efficiency by using significantly fewer frames than larger passive models.

likes.title: Skill-MAS: Evolving Meta-Skill for Automatic Multi-Agent Systems
likes.summary: Skill-MAS introduces a framework for large language model (LLM) based Meta-agents to automatically generate Multi-Agent Systems (MAS). It enables frozen frontier LLMs to progressively learn and refine their orchestration strategies by iteratively evolving a "Meta-Skill" represented as a natural language document, achieving higher performance at a moderate cost compared to existing methods.

likes.title: Large Language Models Do Not Always Need Readable Language
likes.summary: Large Language Models can effectively process and generate textual representations, termed "BabelTele," that are dense and model-readable but lack human readability. This approach significantly compresses context (e.g., 27.9% of original text volume with 99.5% semantic fidelity) while maintaining high performance in downstream tasks, improving efficiency in multi-agent systems, and extending context windows.

likes.title: World Engine: Towards the Era of Post-Training for Autonomous Driving
likes.summary: World Engine presents a generative framework to address the scarcity of safety-critical events in autonomous driving by post-training policies on synthesized, photorealistic, interactive scenarios. This approach improved success rates by 15.23 percentage points on a nuPlan benchmark and reduced pedestrian/cyclist collisions by 15.8% and cut-in collisions by 45.5% in production-scale simulations.

likes.title: Visual-OPSD: Cross-Modal On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient Unified Multimodal Reasoning
likes.summary: Visual-OPSD introduces a cross-modal on-policy self-distillation framework that transfers implicit reasoning knowledge from a model's visual generation pathway to its text-only understanding pathway. This enables efficient unified multimodal reasoning, yielding a 14.3x inference speedup and an average accuracy gain of 3.40 percentage points over its generative teacher on nine benchmarks, with notable improvements in complex spatial reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Rethinking Reward Supervision: Rubric-Conditioned Self-Distillation
likes.summary: Researchers from Yale University developed Rubric-Conditioned Self-Distillation (RCSD), a post-training framework that integrates structured, criterion-level rubrics into token-level self-distillation for language models. This approach achieved an average score of 70.6 on science reasoning benchmarks using Qwen3-8B, outperforming the base model by 4.7 points and the strongest baseline (OPSD) by 0.9 points, particularly excelling in rubric-based reasoning tasks.
